blocks.text: With **TR-069 device management**, the helpdesk sees and fixes a subscriber's home router or ONT remotely. It runs on your own servers, so there is no per-device cloud fee.

Fixed-broadband ISPs pay per device for cloud router management, or run weak tools that leave the helpdesk unable to see Wi-Fi interference or the fiber signal. Mass firmware updates are risky. Router activation is disconnected from the customer's plan.

sections.h2: Router faults found in one click

blocks.text: Your helpdesk runs a one-click health check on the subscriber's router. It names the likely cause and the next step.
Wi-Fi interference and fiber signal are visible from the same screen.
A bad firmware build stops before it reaches every home. Firmware goes out in staged waves. Each wave has a success threshold, and the rollout stops if it is not met.
A bad release reaches a small group of homes first.

sections.h2: Installing Home Router and ONT Management

blocks.text: Your team installs Home Router and ONT Management in containers, one standard way, from the same automated guide as every Alepo product. Upgrades stay small.

When something needs fixing, the patch goes only to the component affected, with rollback ready, so your maintenance window stays short and nothing else has to be upgraded at the same time. Home Router and ONT Management runs on Kubernetes in your environment, operated by your team or by Alepo, with 24x7 support from GTAC.
The build you test and see demoed is the build that goes live.
